label: Zendesk
terms_note: Automation allowed: https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/api/v2/ with API-token Basic auth (email/token:token) or OAuth. POST /api/v2/tickets {ticket{comment{body|html_body, public}, requester_id|requester{name,email}, subject, …}}; PUT /api/v2/tickets/{id} with comment adds a reply (public true) or an internal note (public false); safe_update + updated_stamp prevent collisions; GET /api/v2/tickets (cursor pagination), /api/v2/search. Rate limits per plan: Team 200, Growth / Professional 400, Enterprise 700, Enterprise Plus 2,500 requests / minute (High Volume add-on 2,500); ticket update endpoint 30 updates per 10 minutes per user per ticket and 100 RPM account-wide (300 with High Volume); X-Rate-Limit header, 429 + Retry-After; Zendesk may enforce 100,000 RPM account cap on spikes.

sdks: Zendesk API client libraries (Ruby zendesk_api, Python zenpy community, Node node-zendesk) — developer.zendesk.com

endpoints.purpose: html_body, public: true}, status, assignee_id, safe_update: true, updated_stamp}}`

endpoints.call: Webhooks (Admin Center) fired by triggers / automations on ticket events → our endpoint

reference.limits: - Account-wide per plan: Team 200, Growth / Professional 400, Enterprise 700, Enterprise Plus 2,500 requests / minute (High Volume add-on 2,500); `X-Rate-Limit` header; 429 + `Retry-After`; possible 100,000 RPM protective cap. - Tickets endpoint: **100 RPM (300 with High Volume)** and **30 updates per 10 minutes per user per ticket**. - Automation of the user's own instance is normal Zendesk usage; API token = agent seat's rights.

adapter.rate_note: Account-wide limits by plan (Team 200/min … Enterprise 700/min); Update Ticket has its own limit; HTTP 429 + Retry-After (https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/introduction/rate-limits/).

fields.name: email_token
fields.help: Agent email followed by /token, e.g. jdoe@example.com/token: API-token auth is Basic '{email_address}/token:{api_token}' (https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/introduction/security-and-auth/).

fields.name: api_token
fields.help: API token from Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > Zendesk API.

me.note: Show Self: account.user is the authenticated agent (an anonymous user without id means the credentials were not accepted).

list_inbound.note: Tickets (one row per ticket, most recently updated first; offset pagination, max 100 per page). text is the ticket description (first comment); thread_id is the ticket id for get_thread / reply. `since` is not sent.

get_thread.note: Comments of ticket `thread_id`, oldest first (public replies and internal notes; raw.public tells them apart).

send.note: Creates a ticket with requester `to` (email; Zendesk creates the user if unknown) and `text` as the first comment, which notifies the requester per the account's triggers. message_id is the ticket id.

reply.note: Adds a PUBLIC comment to ticket `thread_id` (Update Ticket with ticket.comment); message_id is the id of the audit the update produced.

not_offered.mark_read: Tickets and comments have no per-agent read state in the Ticketing API (https://developer.zendesk.com/api-reference/ticketing/tickets/tickets/); only ticket status can be changed.
